input.summary: Nine targeted patches across draft/09-claims.md, figures/FIG-1.md, figures/FIG-2.md and figures/FIG-4.md. The mechanical 112(a) check is cleared by replacing "exceeding" with the description's own "being above" in claims 1 and 11 (the condition is unchanged; the description already recites it at staged reduction step 210, so no widening of the description was needed). The five drawing findings are repaired in the figure briefs so the pipeline renders and inspects fresh pixels: FIG. 4 leader endpoints are now specified per shape as interior points clear of the connector arrows and outlines; FIG. 2 numeral 108 is pinned to the solid bus line left of the dashed rectangle and expressly clear of the dashed sensing connection; FIG. 2 numeral 128 is repositioned below the block so its short leader cannot reach or cross the electric vehicle 130, backed by a general rule that no leader may enter another element; FIG. 1 gains an explicit exclusion forbidding any line work below the row of blocks other than the edge controller, the bus with its two branches and the dashed sensing connection, and forbidding a doubled or full-width solid line along the enclosure's lower side; FIG. 1 numeral 106 is moved into the lower right quadrant of the block interior, away from where the dashed sensing connection lands. No claim scope, numeral, embodiment or description passage was altered beyond the one flagged word, and nothing was added from the rendered images. As the brief notes, no prior-art search was run for this application, so the art in prior_art/ may be incomplete and the claims have not been tested against a full search.
changes: draft/09-claims.md claim 1: "responsive to the measured branch current exceeding the branch current limit" changed to "responsive to the measured branch current being above the branch current limit", matching the wording of the detailed description, the summary, the abstract and the disclosure.
draft/09-claims.md claim 11: same change to the corresponding method recitation, clearing the last claim word absent from the specification.

figures/FIG-4.md: the general leader paragraph now requires every leader to end at a point in the interior white space of the shape named for it and forbids endpoints on a shape outline, on a vertical connector line, on an arrowhead or on the square terminator; numerals sit in the white band between the column and the return path on that side.

figures/FIG-4.md numeral list: each of 202, 204, 206, 208, 210, 212, 214 and 216 now states an unambiguous interior endpoint. 202 ends in the lower part of the topmost rectangle below the return-path arrowheads; 204, 206, 208, 212 and 216 end in the left half of their rectangle interiors; 210 ends between the centre of the upper diamond and its right vertex (its left vertex carries the left return path); 214 ends between the centre of the lower diamond and its left vertex (its right vertex carries the branch to the terminator); 216 is additionally kept clear of the return path that starts at the bottom rectangle's right side.

figures/FIG-2.md numeral 108: endpoint tightened to the solid bus line in the portion between the left edge of the drawing area and the left side of the dashed rectangle, expressly clear of the dashed sensing-connection line, so the numeral can no longer land on the sensing connection.

figures/FIG-2.md numeral 128: the numeral is placed below the vehicle connector block and below the lower side of the dashed rectangle, with a short leader rising into the block and expressly not entering or crossing the rounded rectangle of the electric vehicle 130.
figures/FIG-2.md general leader paragraph: added the rule that no leader enters, crosses or touches the outline or interior of any element other than the one it names.

figures/FIG-1.md: added an explicit exclusion that between the row of three blocks and the lower side of the dashed enclosure the only line work is the edge controller block, the isolated local bus and its two rising branches, and the dashed sensing connection; the enclosure's lower side is drawn once as a dashed line, is not doubled by any solid line, and no line runs the full width of the enclosure below the row of blocks.

figures/FIG-1.md numeral 106: endpoint moved to the lower right quadrant of the edge controller block interior, clear of the block outline and clear of the point where the dashed sensing-connection line meets the block.

patches.replace: send a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current being above the branch current limit; and
patches.why: Mechanical claim-support check: "exceeding" appears nowhere in the specification. The description, summary and abstract all state the condition as the measured branch current being above the branch current limit, as does the disclosure. Same condition, description's wording.

patches.replace: sending a reduced pilot command responsive to the measured branch current being above the branch current limit; and
patches.why: Same wording drift in the method claim; aligned with the staged reduction step 210 paragraph of the detailed description.

patches.find: Each of the leftmost and middle blocks meets exactly two lines: a vertical drop at its top edge and a vertical branch at its bottom edge. The rightmost block meets exactly one line: the vertical drop at its top edge.
patches.replace:
Each of the leftmost and middle blocks meets exactly two lines: a vertical drop at its top edge and a vertical branch at its bottom edge. The rightmost block meets exactly one line: the vertical drop at its top edge.

No line work other than the edge controller block, the isolated local bus with its two rising branches, and the dashed sensing-connection line appears between the row of three blocks and the lower side of the dashed enclosing rectangle. The lower side of the dashed enclosing rectangle is drawn once, as a dashed line, and is not doubled or accompanied by any solid line; no line of any kind runs the full width of the enclosure below the row of three blocks, and no line extends to the right of the stated right-hand end of the isolated local bus beneath the middle block.
patches.why: Finding: an undescribed, unnumbered full-width solid horizontal line appears near the bottom of the enclosure. The brief enumerated the line work but never excluded additions, so the exclusion is now explicit for the pipeline to render against.

patches.find: - 106 edge controller: leader ends well inside the lower left block.
patches.replace: - 106 edge controller: leader ends in the interior of the lower left block, in its lower right quadrant, clear of the block outline and clear of the point at which the dashed sensing-connection line meets the top side of the block.
patches.why: Finding: the 106 terminal dot coincided with the landing point of the dashed sensing-connection line on the block outline, so it could read as designating that connection.

patches.find: Each reference numeral sits on a short straight leader clear of the line work and crossing no other leader.
patches.replace: Each reference numeral sits on a short straight leader clear of the line work and crossing no other leader. No leader enters, crosses or touches the outline or the interior of any element other than the one it names, and each leader ends at a single point on the element named for it.
patches.why: Finding: the 128 leader crossed the outline of the electric vehicle 130 twice and traversed its interior. The general rule now forbids a leader passing through any element other than its own.

patches.find: - 108 isolated local bus: leader ends on the bus line left of the dashed rectangle.
patches.replace: - 108 isolated local bus: leader ends on the solid bus line in the portion between the left edge of the drawing area and the left side of the dashed rectangle, clear of the dashed sensing-connection line and clear of every bend in that dashed line.
patches.why: Finding: the 108 terminal dot landed on the bend of the dashed sensing-connection line, which the same brief identifies as a connection separate from the bus, so the numeral labelled the wrong element.

patches.find: - 128 vehicle connector: leader ends well inside the block straddling the right side.
patches.replace: - 128 vehicle connector: the numeral is placed below the vehicle connector block and below the lower side of the dashed rectangle; its leader is short, rises to end well inside the block straddling the right side of the dashed rectangle, and does not enter or cross the rounded rectangle of the electric vehicle.
patches.why: Finding: the 128 numeral sat at the far bottom right and its long diagonal leader ran through the interior of the electric vehicle 130. Repositioning the numeral makes a short leader that cannot reach the vehicle.

patches.find: Part names below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each numeral sits on a short straight leader clear of the line work, crossing no other leader, and ending well inside the shape named for it.
patches.replace: Part names below are semantic identifiers only and do not appear as drawing text. Each numeral sits in the white space beside the column, between the column and the return path on that side, close to the shape it names, and is joined to that shape by a short straight leader that crosses no other leader and no line work. Every leader ends at a point lying in the interior white space of the shape named for it, well within that shape's outline. No leader ends on the outline of a shape, on a vertical connector line, on an arrowhead, on a return path or on the square terminator, and no leader ends in the white gap between two shapes.
patches.why: Finding: in the render the terminal dots for 210, 212, 214 and 216 sat on connector arrows and shape edges rather than inside the shapes, so 214 landed on shape 212 and 216 landed on shape 214. The general rule now states the requirement unambiguously and names the forbidden endpoints.

- 206 pilot command step: leader ends well inside the third shape from the top.
- 208 connector verification step: leader ends well inside the fourth shape from the top.
- 210 staged reduction step: leader ends well inside the upper of the two diamonds.
- 212 ordered shedding step: leader ends well inside the rectangle that lies between the two diamonds.
- 214 welded-contactor isolation step: leader ends well inside the lower of the two diamonds.
- 216 conditional reclosure step: leader ends well inside the bottom rectangle.
patches.replace:
- 202 available current determination step: leader ends inside the topmost rectangle, in the lower part of its interior, below the mid height at which the two return-path arrowheads touch its sides, and clear of the rectangle outline, of those two arrowheads and of the vertical connector line leaving its lower edge.
- 204 sustaining and deficit assignment step: leader ends inside the second shape from the top, which is a rectangle, in the left half of its interior, clear of the rectangle outline and of the vertical connector lines above and below it.
- 206 pilot command step: leader ends inside the third shape from the top, which is a rectangle, in the left half of its interior, clear of the rectangle outline and of the vertical connector lines above and below it.
- 208 connector verification step: leader ends inside the fourth shape from the top, which is a rectangle, in the left half of its interior, clear of the rectangle outline and of the vertical connector lines above and below it.
- 210 staged reduction step: leader ends inside the upper of the two diamonds, between the centre of that diamond and its right vertex, clear of the diamond outline, of the vertical connector lines at its upper and lower vertices and of the left return path leaving its left vertex.
- 212 ordered shedding step: leader ends inside the rectangle that lies between the two diamonds, in the left half of its interior, clear of the rectangle outline and of the vertical connector lines above and below it, and not in the white gap between that rectangle and either diamond.

# FIG. 1

A flat schematic system diagram in plain black line work on white, no shading and no words other than the reference numerals below. All line work stays clear of the filing margins.

A dashed rectangle encloses the whole diagram and is the charging installation. Inside it, one horizontal solid line across the upper part is the branch conductor; its left end stops exactly at the left side of the dashed rectangle, without crossing it, and its right end stops short of the right side, above the rightmost block below.

An empty rectangle in the left portion of this line is the branch current sensor; the line passes through it at its vertical centre, entering the middle of its left side and leaving the middle of its right side. This rectangle lies entirely left of the leftmost block below.

Three identical empty rectangular blocks stand in a row across the lower part, plainly spaced apart, their top edges at one height and their bottom edges at one height: the leftmost a first connector channel, the middle a second connector channel, the rightmost a non-charging load. A short vertical line drops from the horizontal line to the top edge of each, connecting the three in parallel, all three drops lying right of the branch current sensor.

A further empty rectangular block below the row and toward the left of the drawing area is the edge controller; its top side lies below the bottom edges of the three blocks and its right side left of the leftmost block.

A solid line leaves the right side of the edge controller block and runs horizontally beneath the leftmost and middle blocks as an isolated local bus, ending beneath the middle block. A short vertical branch rises from this bus to the bottom edge of the leftmost block and another to the bottom edge of the middle block. The rightmost block meets only its top drop.

A dashed sensing-connection line joins the branch current sensor to the edge controller in three straight segments: down from the middle of the bottom side of the sensor rectangle, then left, then down to a point on the top side of the edge controller block.

A flat block diagram of the edge controller in plain black line work on white, no shading and no words in the drawing area other than the reference numerals below, all line work clear of the filing margins.

One large rectangle occupies the left and central portion of the drawing area and is the edge controller. Three smaller empty rectangles lie inside it: one in the upper region, the network interface; one in the lower region, the nonvolatile memory; and one in the left region, the service input. Single verified finding: the FIG-1 brief exceeds the 2,800-character drawing-brief cap by a redundant geometry clause. One patch to the authoritative Markdown brief resolves it; no rendered artifact is touched, and the drawing pipeline will re-render and re-inspect from the corrected brief.

The deleted clause is pure restatement — "the line passes through it at its vertical centre" already fixes where the branch conductor enters and leaves the sensor rectangle, so every part, connection, relative position and numeral of FIG. 1 is unchanged. Nothing in `draft/07-drawings.md`, `draft/08-detailed-description.md`, `draft/numerals.md` or the claims describes that entry/exit wording, so no companion patch is required to keep them synchronized.

Note carried forward from the brief: no prior-art search was run, so the art considered may be incomplete.

input.summary: Fixed the one open gate item: figures/FIG-1.md sat at or above the 2,800-character drawing-brief cap. Deleted the 78-character redundant clause in the branch-current-sensor sentence identified by the report, bringing the brief to roughly 2,731 characters of content (about 2,758 with line breaks), safely under the maximum. The clause only restated geometry already fixed by the preceding clause of the same sentence, so all parts, connections, relative positions and numerals of FIG. 1 are unchanged and no synchronized change to the numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description or claims is needed. The source-fidelity ledger reported no unsupported content, so no other file was altered; everything else is kept byte for byte. The corrected brief must be re-rendered and re-inspected by the drawing pipeline before publication. Per the drafting brief, no prior-art search was run and the art available may be incomplete.

No other file changed: the numeral table, drawing descriptions, detailed description, claims, abstract and the FIG-2 through FIG-4 briefs are untouched, as the removed clause has no counterpart in any of them and the gate report recorded no other verified finding.
